svg.text: An exact circle-domain model of a 5-connected domain
the Joukowski map J(z) = z + 1/z is one-to-one on |z| > 1, so it carries the circle domain D conformally onto G
G = J(D): a slit, three ovals, one point
unit disk, three round disks, one point
Grey curves: circles |z| = r and rays in D, and their images (confocal ellipses and hyperbolas, foci at -2 and 2) in G.
Checks (11642 sample points with |z| > 1): max |J⁻¹(J(z)) - z| = 1.9e-14; slit flatness max |Im J| on |z| = 1: 2.2e-16;
roundness max/min radius from centroid: source disks 1.0000, image ovals 1.098, 1.121, 1.099.
This finitely connected case is Koebe's classical theorem; the picture illustrates the statement and proves nothing new.
